An active monitoring tool reports that the link successfully delivers 850 Mbps of user data, while the one-way transit delay is measured at 12 milliseconds. Which statement correctly maps these values to the fundamental network metrics of nominal capacity, application goodput, and one-way latency?

Una herramienta de monitoreo activo informa que el enlace entrega con éxito 850 Mbps de datos de usuario, mientras que el retardo de tránsito unidireccional se mide en 12 milisegundos. ¿Qué afirmación asigna correctamente estos valores a las métricas fundamentales de red de capacidad nominal, goodput de aplicación y latencia unidireccional?

The 850 Mb/s of delivered application payload is application goodput; a throughput measurement must state the protocol layer and bytes counted. The 12 ms value is one-way latency, not delay variation (jitter). The measurements alone do not identify why the payload rate is below nominal link capacity.

questions.statementEn: Assume an ordinary unicast data packet with a valid source and no ICMP-error suppression or rate limiting. A router receives an IPv4 packet with a total length of 1500 bytes on an Ethernet interface. The routing table indicates that the packet must exit an outgoing interface where the IP MTU is configured as 1400 bytes. The IP header has the Don't Fragment (DF) bit set to 1. What action does the router take, and what message does it send to the originating host?
questions.statementEs: Supón un paquete de datos unicast ordinario con origen válido y sin supresión ni límites de tasa para errores ICMP. Un router recibe un paquete IPv4 con una longitud total de 1500 bytes en una interfaz Ethernet. La tabla de enrutamiento indica que el paquete debe salir por una interfaz de salida donde la IP MTU está configurada en 1400 bytes. El encabezado IP tiene el bit Don't Fragment (DF) establecido en 1. ¿Qué acción realiza el router y qué mensaje envía al host de origen?
questions.explanationEn: The 1500-byte IPv4 packet exceeds MTU 1400 and DF prohibits router fragmentation, so it is discarded. For the stated ordinary unicast packet, absent ICMP suppression or rate limits, the router reports ICMP type 3 code 4 with next-hop MTU 1400. PMTUD lets the sender adjust packetization; it does not require changing the already-negotiated TCP MSS option, and the packet need not even contain TCP.

Para el paquete unicast ordinario indicado, sin supresión ni límites ICMP, el router comunica ICMP tipo 3 código 4 con MTU de siguiente salto 1400. PMTUD permite ajustar la formación de paquetes; no exige modificar la opción MSS TCP ya negociada, y el paquete ni siquiera tiene que transportar TCP.

questions.statementEn: For IPv4 multicast group addressing described in RFC 1112 (historically called Class D), which address range and high-order bit pattern apply?

questions.statementEn: In IEEE 802.11ax (Wi-Fi 6), which physical/MAC layer technology enables an Access Point to divide a single wireless channel (such as 20 MHz or 80 MHz) into smaller groups of subcarriers called Resource Units (RUs), enabling simultaneous parallel communication with multiple client devices in both downlink and uplink directions?

questions.explanationEn: OFDMA allocates resource units, each consisting of a group of subcarriers, to multiple users within a transmission opportunity. Wi-Fi 6 supports downlink and uplink OFDMA with suitable AP/client support. MU-MIMO separates users spatially and can complement OFDMA; 802.11ac already supported downlink MU-MIMO, so it is incorrect to say every prior transmission served exactly one user. OFDMA can improve dense-network efficiency but does not guarantee a latency reduction for every workload.

MU-MIMO separa usuarios espacialmente y puede complementar OFDMA; 802.11ac ya admitía MU-MIMO descendente, por lo que no es correcto afirmar que toda transmisión anterior atendía exactamente a un usuario. Allow probe/track timers to expire. A branch office router connects to the internet via a primary fiber WAN link and a backup 4G LTE router. If an upstream ISP provider outage occurs beyond the local fiber gateway, the local Ethernet link status to the modem remains UP/UP, preventing traditional static route failover. How can an administrator combine Cisco IP Service Level Agreements (IP SLA) with Object Tracking to solve this problem?

Deja vencer los temporizadores de sonda y tracking. Un router de sucursal se conecta a internet mediante un enlace WAN de fibra principal y un router 4G LTE de respaldo. Si ocurre una interrupción del proveedor ISP aguas arriba más allá de la pasarela de fibra local, el estado del enlace Ethernet local hacia el módem permanece UP/UP, impidiendo la conmutación por error tradicional de la ruta estática. ¿Cómo puede un administrador combinar Cisco IP Service Level Agreements (IP SLA) con Object Tracking para resolver este problema?
questions.explanationEn: An IP SLA probe can test a target beyond the primary gateway; a tracking object can condition installation of the primary static route. A higher-distance backup is usable only if its next hop is independently resolvable. Probe routing/source selection must continue testing the intended primary path after failover, otherwise a response through the backup can cause misleading recovery. Detection follows probe timeout and tracking timers. An ICMP failure may be filtering or target failure rather than complete service loss; existing application sessions may need separate recovery.

La ruta y origen de la sonda deben seguir probando el camino principal previsto tras conmutar, pues una respuesta por el respaldo puede simular una recuperación. La detección depende del timeout y temporizadores. questions.statementEn: An attacker connects a rogue laptop running a MAC address flooding tool (`macof`) to switch port FastEthernet0/10, transmitting thousands of spoofed Ethernet frames per second with random source MAC addresses. The switch's CAM table fills completely, increasing unknown-unicast flooding in the affected VLAN. Which Cisco switch feature mitigates this attack, and how do the `protect` and `restrict` violation modes differ when an unauthorized MAC address is detected?
questions.statementEs: Un atacante conecta una computadora portátil no autorizada que ejecuta una herramienta de inundación de direcciones MAC (`macof`) al puerto del switch FastEthernet0/10, transmitiendo miles de tramas Ethernet falsificadas por segundo con direcciones MAC de origen aleatorias. La tabla CAM del switch se llena por completo, aumentando el flooding unicast desconocido en la VLAN afectada. ¿Qué característica del switch Cisco mitiga este ataque y en qué se diferencian los modos de violación `protect` y `restrict` cuando se detecta una dirección MAC no autorizada?
questions.explanationEn: Exhausting dynamic learning can increase unknown-unicast flooding, subject to VLAN membership, forwarding state and suppression policies; known destinations need not be flooded and the switch does not become a physical hub. Port security limits permitted source MAC learning on a suitable access port. Protect drops violating frames without the restrict-mode counter/notification behavior; restrict drops and counts violations and generates supported notification events. A network security engineer enables Dynamic ARP Inspection (DAI) on access switch SW1 for VLAN 10 using `ip arp inspection vlan 10`. DHCP Snooping is enabled, and untrusted access ports connect workstations. While workstations with dynamic DHCP addresses communicate normally, several critical servers with statically configured IPv4 addresses lose network reachability. The switch console generates repeated error logs:
`%SW_DAI-4-DHCP_SNOOPING_DENY: 1 Invalid ARPs (Req) on Fa0/24, vlan 10: [0050.56a0.1111/192.168.10.50/0000.0000.0000/192.168.10.1]`
What is the root cause of this connectivity loss, and how is it resolved?
questions.statementEs:
Se verifica que este servidor estático no tiene una asociación snooping aplicable ni un permiso de ACL ARP. Un ingeniero de seguridad de redes habilita Dynamic ARP Inspection (DAI) en el switch de acceso SW1 para la VLAN 10 utilizando `ip arp inspection vlan 10`. DHCP Snooping está habilitado y los puertos de acceso no confiables conectan estaciones de trabajo. Mientras que las estaciones con direcciones DHCP dinámicas se comunican normalmente, varios servidores críticos con direcciones IPv4 configuradas estáticamente pierden la alcanzabilidad de red. La consola del switch genera repetidos registros de error:
`%SW_DAI-4-DHCP_SNOOPING_DENY: 1 Invalid ARPs (Req) on Fa0/24, vlan 10: [0050.56a0.1111/192.168.10.50/0000.0000.0000/192.168.10.1]`
¿Cuál es la causa raíz de esta pérdida de conectividad y cómo se resuelve?

An appropriately scoped ARP ACL permitting the legitimate IP/MAC pair and applied with ip arp inspection filter can resolve this case. Static addressing does not logically prohibit manual bindings or other supported designs. Keep validation on untrusted host ports; making every server port trusted/trunked is not a required fix.

VLAN hopping is a Layer 2 attack technique that enables an attacker on one VLAN to inject unauthorized traffic into another VLAN. Which two configuration measures effectively mitigate both Dynamic Trunking Protocol (DTP) switch spoofing and 802.1Q double-tagging attacks across enterprise access switches? (Choose two.)
questions.statementEs: Evalúa mitigación de las condiciones clásicas de suplantación de switch y doble etiqueta en VLAN nativa, no una garantía contra toda vulnerabilidad VLAN posible. VLAN hopping es una técnica de ataque de Capa 2 que permite a un atacante en una VLAN inyectar tráfico no autorizado hacia otra VLAN. ¿Cuáles dos medidas de configuración mitigan eficazmente tanto los ataques de switch spoofing por Dynamic Trunking Protocol (DTP) como los de doble etiquetado 802.1Q a través de switches de acceso empresariales? (Elija dos.)
questions.explanationEn: Static access mode and disabling DTP on untrusted user ports prevent trunk negotiation through switch spoofing. In the classic double-tagging scenario, forwarding removes the outer tag associated with the native VLAN and leaves the inner tag visible to the next switch; the wire frame is not simply tag-free. Using a consistent unused native VLAN that no user access port inhabits removes a key condition of that classic attack. Native tagging and platform handling provide additional protections; do not assume one control defeats every possible VLAN-escape flaw.

questions.explanationEn: The configured native VLAN IDs differ: SW-1 uses 10 and SW-2 uses 20. PVID-inconsistent is not a synonym for type-inconsistent. DTP does not automatically align native VLAN IDs.

questions.statementEn: An IP SLA operation is configured as icmp-echo to 203.0.113.1. An ISP filter drops those echo requests while HTTP/HTTPS through the primary gateway still works. Lab checks explicitly show track 1 DOWN, withdrawal of the tracked primary default and installation of a valid backup via 198.51.100.2. Which conclusion about this availability signal is justified?
questions.statementEs: Una operación IP SLA está configurada como icmp-echo a 203.0.113.1. Un filtro ISP descarta esas solicitudes mientras HTTP/HTTPS por el gateway principal sigue funcionando. Las comprobaciones de laboratorio muestran explícitamente track 1 DOWN, retiro de la default principal seguida e instalación de un respaldo válido vía 198.51.100.2. ¿Qué conclusión sobre esta señal de disponibilidad está justificada?
questions.explanationEn: The operation tests ICMP echo reachability, not the HTTP application. Here the lab explicitly observes track 1 down, primary-route withdrawal and backup-route installation. Filtering only ICMP can therefore cause the observed false-negative signal even while HTTP through the primary path works. This observation does not prove that IP SLA inspected passing TCP, that both unequal-distance defaults load-balance, or that the physical interface became err-disabled. Probe choice should match the availability being monitored.
